title: WPPIL/64/2024 of ABHINAV CHAUDHARY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPPIL No. 64 of 2024
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
 Mr. Navnish Negi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate
General for the State.
3. This writ petition has been filed in public
interest seeking the following reliefs:-
"(i) To issue writ, order and direction in the
nature of Mandamus Commanding Respondent
No. 1 to Initiate a High Level Independent
Enquiry into the Allotment of Tender to
Respondent no. 3 and to take appropriate
Legal action against the Delinquent Officials in
accordance with law."
4. According to the petitioner, certain
irregularities were committed in procurement
of 95 vertical stationary hydraulic compactor
machines by respondent no. 2.
5. Learned State Counsel, on instructions,
submits that e-tenders were invited on
Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal for
procurement of compactors on 14.09.2022.
Technical bids of following six bidders were
received in response to the e-tender, out of
which, first three bidders were declared to be
technically qualified.:-
(1) Indian Reflective Center, Meerut.
(2) Steel Fabs, Dehradun.
(3) JMK facilities, Gaziabad.
(4) Duo Machines corps, Rajkot

(5) J.K. Lathe Spares
(6) Soham Impex, Rajkot
6. He further submits that purchase order
was issued to the lowest bidder i.e.
respondent no. 3, who had offered
compactor at the rate of Rs. 5,23,500/- per
piece. He further submits that out of the 95
compactors supplied by respondent no. 3, 88
have been subjected to third party
inspection. He, thus, submits that this is a
motivated writ petition filed with oblique
motive.
7. We find some force in the contention
raised by learned State Counsel that writ
petition appears to have been filed at the
behest of an unsuccessful bidder.
8. Even otherwise also, the process of
procurement was over in the year 2022,
there is no explanation offered by petitioner
for approaching this Court after such delay.
Even otherwise also, procurement was made
through Government e-market place portal in
which there is remote possibility of such
irregularities, as indicated by the petitioner.
9. Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is
dismissed.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 12.04.2024
U.U.
